VBSC 50.name: Mechanisms of Disease
VBSC 50.description: First-Year Seminar introducing the study of disease pathogenesis and careers in animal health research and service.

VBSC 211.name: The Immune System and Disease
VBSC 211.description: Introduction to the immune system, emphasizing the immune response to infection and consequences of a defective immune response.

VBSC 410.name: Principles of Immunology
VBSC 410.description: Antigen recognition and innate immune responses to the development of acquired immunity. Cross-listed with MICRB 410.

VBSC 418.name: Bacterial Pathogenesis
VBSC 418.description: Molecular interactions between bacterial pathogens and their hosts.

VBSC 432.name: Advanced Immunology: Signaling in the Immune System
VBSC 432.description: Signaling pathways that regulate the immune response.

VBSC 435.name: Viral Pathogenesis
VBSC 435.description: General knowledge of medically relevant viruses, with a specific focus on important human viral pathogens.

VBSC 444.name: Epidemiology of Infectious Diseases
VBSC 444.description: Core epidemiologic concepts of infectious diseases and methods for disease identification and prevention.

VBSC 445.name: Molecular Epidemiology of Infectious Diseases
VBSC 445.description: Discussion and practicum of the molecular laboratory techniques used to study molecular epidemiology of infectious diseases.

VBSC 448W.name: Current Topics in Immunology
VBSC 448W.description: Current approaches and questions driving research in immunology and infectious diseases. Writing Across the Curriculum.

VBSC 451.name: Immunotoxicology of Drugs and Chemicals
VBSC 451.description: Effects of chemicals in the environment and the impact of other factors such as therapeutics, recreational drugs, and dietary factors on the immune system.

VBSC 190.name: Careers in Veterinary and Biomedical Sciences
VBSC 190.description: Career strategic planning and opportunities for Veterinary and Biomedical Sciences.

VBSC 230.name: The Science of Poisons
VBSC 230.description: Introduction to toxicology examining how toxic agents affect living organisms through real-world examples.

VBSC 331.name: Pharmacology I: Drug Actions and Reactions
VBSC 331.description: Fundamental principles of pharmacology and mechanisms of drug action. Enforced prerequisite at enrollment: BIOL 230W or BIOL 230M.

VBSC 430.name: Principles of Toxicology
VBSC 430.description: Introduction to the biomedical aspects of toxicology, with emphasis on the mechanisms and fate of chemical interaction with biological systems. Bulletin prereq is '(BIOL 110 and BIOL 240W) or BMB 211 or BMB 401' -- BIOL 110 is a universal entrance requirement for this major, so the effective gate is BMB 211/401/BIOL 240W.

VBSC 431.name: Environmental Toxicology
VBSC 431.description: Effects of pollutants on animal health at the chemical, physical, and cellular level. Cross-listed with ERM 431.

VBSC 433.name: Molecular and Cellular Toxicology
VBSC 433.description: In-depth coverage of drug/chemical interactions with biological systems and experimental approaches. Cross-listed with BMB 433.

VBSC 438.name: Introduction to Molecular Pharmacology
VBSC 438.description: Correlates chemistry and biochemistry knowledge to understanding drug actions and molecular interactions. Bulletin lists CHEM 202/201 as the prereq; CHEM 210 is treated as equivalent here since the bulletin itself notes CHEM 202 and CHEM 210 duplicate subject matter and cannot both be taken for credit.

VBSC 421.name: Comparative Anatomy of Vertebrates
VBSC 421.description: Vertebrate anatomy from evolutionary and developmental perspectives, studying important structures, terminology, and function across representative groups including fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals.

VBSC 403.name: Principles of Animal Disease Control
VBSC 403.description: Principles of disease control based on knowledge of the multiple causes of animal disease.
